headline: Coastal Access and Barrier Island Ferries
reservation: Ship Island excursions require ferry tickets which should be booked in advance during summer and spring breaks via the official concessionaire. Coastal camping at Davis Bayou is managed through Recreation.gov; check for seasonal availability as some services may scale back in winter months.

days.title: Islands and Marine Life

stops.name: Ship Island
stops.detail: Take the ferry to this barrier island for pristine beaches and a visit to the historic Fort Massachusetts.

stops.name: Mississippi Aquarium
stops.detail: Explore regional aquatic habitats and learn about Gulf conservation efforts in downtown Gulfport.

days.driving: Walking to ferry; local transfer to aquarium
days.note: Ferry service is weather-dependent and typically does not operate in winter.

days.title: Bayous and Artistic Villages

stops.name: Davis Bayou Area
stops.detail: Part of the Gulf Islands National Seashore, offering marshes, wood duck ponds, and birdwatching trails.

stops.name: Walter Anderson Museum of Art
stops.detail: Discover the works of a local master who captured the ecology of the Mississippi coast.

days.driving: Allow 30-45 minutes; coastal traffic can be slow in downtown districts
days.note: Check tide charts if planning to explore marsh boardwalks during storm surges.

days.title: Coastal Heritage and Sound Views

stops.name: Biloxi Lighthouse
stops.detail: A signature landmark offering guided tours and views over the Mississippi Sound.

stops.name: Maritime & Seafood Industry Museum
stops.detail: Understand the deep history of the Gulf's fishing industry and local wooden boat building.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes; Highway 90 is the main coastal artery
days.note: Sun protection is essential even on overcast days due to water reflection.

intel.title: Public Beach Access
intel.text: Parking along Highway 90 is generally ample but fills quickly during major events like Cruisin' The Coast. Use designated bays to avoid soft sand hazards.

intel.title: Urban Connectivity
intel.text: Cell service is strong throughout the mainland coastal strip. Signals may weaken significantly when traveling by ferry to the outer barrier islands.

intel.title: Mainland Availability
intel.text: Fuel stations are frequent along the Highway 90 corridor and I-10. No fuel or services are available once you depart on the ferry for the islands.

intel.title: Hurricane Season
intel.text: Travel between June and November requires monitoring the National Hurricane Center. Afternoon thunderstorms are common in summer and may cause short ferry delays.

intel.title: Barrier Island Transit
intel.text: Access to Ship Island is only via ferry or private boat. There are no bridges connecting the mainland to the primary recreational barrier islands.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at GPT and head to Ocean Springs or Biloxi for check-in; most coastal amenities are within a 20-minute drive of the terminal.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are ideal for the paved coastal highways. RVs are common but should check height clearances for historic district trees in Ocean Springs.
plan.goldenHour: The Biloxi Lighthouse area provides a clear view of the sound for sunset, with lighting varying by seasonal humidity.
